title: Voiding an Approval and Withdrawing a Request — Prior Authorization Terms
content:
**Terms.** A Prairie Ridge Health Plan member may have a Prior Authorization approval voided when the service will not be used, and units already used are never reversed by a void. The member may withdraw an undecided request at any time before the decision; a withdrawn request has no decision and gives no appeal rights. A voided or withdrawn authorization is never reopened; a later need is a new request.

**Retired wording.** The clause that "the units left are released the same day where the class releases units on a void" is **no longer in force**. The units a void releases are governed by the plan's current basis for voiding an approval.

The class setting this rule reads is whether a void releases the approval's unused units.

## Void and withdrawal side by side

| | Void | Withdrawal |
|---|---|---|
| Applies to | an approval | an undecided request |
| When | when the service will not be used | at any time before the decision |
| Units already used | never reversed by the void | — |
| Decision and appeal rights | — | no decision and no appeal rights |
| Reopening | never reopened; a later need is a new request | never reopened; a later need is a new request |

## Basis questions

**Can a member bring back a voided approval if the service is needed after all?** No. A voided authorization is never reopened; the later need is a new request.

**Does withdrawing a request leave the member able to appeal it?** No. A withdrawn request has no decision and gives no appeal rights.

**Hypothetical case.** A hypothetical member used 4 visits of an approval and then has it voided: the 4 visits used stay used; the void never reverses them.

superseded_clauses: the units left are released the same day where void_releases_units is true
